 Twins, Dodgers Swap Royce Lewis For Bobby Miller
 By Steve Adams |
 at November 20, 2026 4:48pm CDT 
 4:48pm: Right-hander and former top prospect Bobby Miller is also headed to Minnesota in the deal, reports Robert Murray of FanSided.
 4:27pm: The Dodgers have acquired infielder Royce Lewis from the Twins, reports Jon Heyman of The New York Post . Los Angeles has open 40-man spots and won’t need to make a corresponding move. The Twins receive minor league catcher Francisco Espinoza in return, per Heyman .
 Lewis, 27, was the No. 1 overall pick in the 2017 draft and at one point ranked among the game’s very best prospects. He climbed through the Twins’ system as a shortstop but largely settled in at third base. At various points early on in his career, the righty-swinging slugger looked primed for stardom. Lewis was an absolute monster during the Twins’ playoff push in 2023, hitting .309/.372/.548 with 15 homers in 239 plate appearances that were scattered around multiple IL stints. He went 5-for-22 with four home runs, including a grand slam, during Minnesota’s ALDS run that year.
 Unfortunately, that injury caveat has been far, far too prominent a concern in Lewis’ career. He’s amassed nearly five full years of major league service time but has only 1517 plate appearances. Lewis has twice torn the ACL in his right knee, and he’s been on the major league injured list a whopping 11 times due almost entirely to various leg injuries — most of them hamstring and quadriceps strains of varying degrees.
 As Lewis has continually incurred knee, hamstring and quad injuries, his athleticism has slipped. He opened the 2026 season at his customary third base but was optioned in May amid alarming struggles at the plate; Lewis slashed just .163/.261/.279 with a 31% strikeout rate through his first 119 turns at the plate. While he was in Triple-A, Minnesota moved Brooks Lee from shortstop to third base. Lee not only saw his offense pick up with the position swap but settled in as one of the best defensive third basemen in the league, finishing out the season as an American League Gold Glove finalist.
 Lewis returned after just over two weeks — not because the Twins needed to fill in for an injury but rather because he utterly obliterated Triple-A opposition. He played in 15 games, totaled 60 plate appearances and ripped 10 homers while batting .333/.403/.900.
 The brief reset looked to have done wonders when Lewis was first recalled. He shifted across the diamond to first and second base (more of the former) and roared out of the gates with a .280/.344/.498 batting line across his next 250 plate appearances — all while walking at an 8.8% clip and fanning in a greatly reduced 23.2% of his plate appearances. Lewis then fell into another swoon, hitting .187/.207/.261 over his final 140 plate appearances. He ended the year with a lackluster .227/.287/.380 line — about 15% worse than league average, by measure of wRC+.
 Lewis now heads to his native Southern California as a pure change-of-scenery candidate. He hit .307/.364/.549 over his first 280 plate appearances in 2022-23 but has mustered just a .232/.288/.401 slash in 1237 plate appearances since. He can probably still handle third base on a part-time basis but is better suited for work at less demanding positions. He’s projected by MLBTR contributor Matt Swartz to earn a $5.1MM salary next year.
 In Los Angeles, Lewis can spell lefty-swinging Max Muncy and Freddie Freeman at the corners and perhaps take some reps at second base. He posted slightly above-average numbers against lefties in 2026 and has solid numbers against them in his career overall. Through 2024, he posted solid numbers against righties, but Lewis has been about 20% worse than average in right-on-right situations since 2025.
 More to come.
